Introduction

This buyer guide provides contracting authorities with guidance on how to access and use the Event Management Framework 1 (EMF1).

EMF1 has been established by the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) to provide a compliant, efficient and flexible route to market for a broad range of event management services.

This guide explains:

what services are in scope and can be purchased through EMF1

the available buying options

social value and KPI considerations

Key Information

Category Description

Agreement ID 104209

Agreement name Event Management Framework 1

Agreement type Closed Framework

Relevant legislation Procurement Act 2023

Agreement duration 4 years (optional +1+1)

Start date 1 November 2026

End date 30 October 2030 (or 30 October 2032)

Maximum call-off contract length Call-off contracts may extend beyond the framework expiry date, but must not exceed 24 months following the end of the framework term.

Scope of the agreement This framework enables government to commission event management services.

Buying options Competitive Selection Process, Expedited Competitive Selection Process and Direct Award (where applicable).

Can be used by DCMS, Arm’s Length Bodies (ALBs), Other Government Departments (OGDs) and public sector Contracting Authorities.

Contract notice Link once awarded

Contact details DCMS Commercial Mailbox

Agreement scope and lots

EMF1 provides buyers with access to suppliers capable of delivering a wide range of event management services across 5 lots.

The framework covers both strategic and operational event delivery requirements, ranging from nationally significant events through to smaller community and stakeholder engagement activities.

Buyers should review the lot descriptions before commencing a procurement exercise.

Lot Lot name Lot description

1 National, public-facing events This lot includes large-scale, high-profile and nationally significant events such as:

- royal funerals coronations

- royal weddings

- commemorative events

- nationally significant public-facing occasions

These events typically involve significant public visibility, operational complexity and reputational risk.

Typical services and skills:

- strategic and operational event planning

- end-to-end event orchestration

- programme and delivery oversight

- coordination of third-party suppliers and delivery partners

- supply chain access and assurance

- stakeholder and reputation management

2 Medium to large indoor events This lot includes formal gatherings and engagement events such as:

- ministerial summits

- intergovernmental meetings

- conferences

- diplomatic events

- hybrid and virtual events

These events are designed to support policy, diplomacy, collaboration and strategic engagement.

Typical services and skills:

- venue sourcing and logistics management

- delegate and VIP management

- protocol management and access control

- event production and programme delivery

- digital and hybrid event integration

3 Presence at 3rd party events This lot includes exhibitions and engagement-focused events such as:

- trade shows

- exhibitions and trade fairs

- seminars and roundtables

- webinars

- experiential events

- meet-and-greet sessions

Typical services and skills:

- creative design and branding

- stand design and build

- stakeholder, sponsor and delegate management

- on-site logistics coordination

- visitor experience design

- security and compliance management

4 Small events This lot includes smaller-scale events and activities, typically lasting less than one day, such as:

- receptions

- briefings

- speeches

- community engagement events

- stakeholder gatherings

Typical services and skills

- event production and delivery

- equipment hire and setup

- responsive logistics management

- supplier coordination

5 Event assurance services This lot provides specialist advisory and assurance support during the planning and prospective stages of an event.

Typical services and skills:

- feasibility studies

- deliverability assessments

- crowd assurance and crowd dynamic modelling

- crowd psychology and crowd management expertise

- accessibility expertise

- testing and exercising
